question: Why is the thermal conversion of H2B-SiH2 to Si (μ-H2) BH2 not feasible, and what makes the reverse reaction more feasible?
answer: The thermal conversion of H₂B-SiH₂ (IM2) to Si(μ-H₂)BH₂ (IM4) is not feasible due to two high energy barriers that must be overcome, making the reaction pathway energetically unfavorable. In contrast, the reverse thermal reaction from IM4 to IM2 is more feasible because it involves only one significant barrier. Photochemically, however, IM2 can convert to IM4 under UV irradiation (300–350 nm) due to excitation to the optically accessible D₂ state (3.69 eV), followed by a reaction pathway involving two successive conical intersections (CIs). The BSiH₄ bending mode facilitates the transition by lifting the degeneracy at the second CI, enabling photochemical conversion despite the thermal infeasibility. Computational results confirm these mechanisms and align with experimental observations.
